title: Strip a kale leaf from its stalk
instruction: Strip the kale leaf from its tough stalk. Leave the usable leaf on the board and the stalk separate.
setup: One fresh Tuscan kale leaf, about 270 mm long and 80 mm wide, with a 5–6 mm stalk and 45 mm of bare stalk at its base; a 320 x 340 x 20 mm wooden chopping board. The leaf lies flat, stalk base toward the left arm, tip toward the right. Both hands start open. Use washable food-safe pad covers.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 90% of the leaf area has been stripped and retained on the board, the intact stalk is at least 2 cm clear of the leaf, and both hands have released for three seconds. 0.5 for at least 75% stripped and retained; 0.25 for at least 50% stripped and retained on the board. Otherwise 0. A broken stalk scores 0. Compare before/after photographs on a centimetre grid.
fidelity: Native contact grips a jointed stalk and flexible leaf panels. Weaker leaf-to-stalk bonds break under load; the leaf remains physical matter and falls or stays in the grippers. Stronger stalk and leaf seams can also fail. Geometry, stiffness and tear loads are coarse uncalibrated approximations. Native demo reaches full score using contact grasps.
context: Preparing kale means separating edible leaf tissue from its fibrous stalk without throwing the leaf away with it.
reset_notes: Choose fresh mature Tuscan kale from one batch, 250–290 mm long, with an intact stalk and no missing leaf patches. Trim the bare stalk to 45 mm; wash and pat dry. Photograph it on the grid, then restore the fixed layout. Use a fresh leaf each trial.
